chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Bakr ibn Salih al-Razi, on the authority of Abu Salt al-Haravy, who said: 'I asked Al-Ridha (peace be upon him) about faith.'
He replied, 'Faith is a conviction of the heart, a verbal expression of the tongue, and an action of the limbs; faith is nothing else.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three components of faith according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* articulates the Shia doctrine of *Iman* as a holistic unity of belief, declaration, and action, distinguishing it from views that isolate conviction from practice. By citing the Sixth Imam, al-Rida, the text underscores that true faith is manifested through the integration of the heart, tongue, and limbs, a framework essential for understanding spiritual integrity in Shia jurisprudence and theology.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-240 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Bakr ibn Salih al-Razi, on the authority of Abu Salt al-Haravy, “I asked Al-Ridha (MGB) about faith.
The Imam (MGB) replied, ‘Faith consists of whole-hearted acceptance, verbal expression, and acting accordingly. Faith is nothing else.’”
